name: Musical instrument practice
description: A steady practice plan for any instrument: sound, technique, reading, rhythm, ear training and repertoire. It has no end date; it is a habit that grows with you, measured by weekly practice time.

steps.title: Set up your instrument and practice space
steps.description: Get the instrument in good playing condition and tuned. Add a metronome, a tuner, a music stand, a recorder and a fixed place and time to practise.

steps.title: Posture, holding and producing a clean sound
steps.description: Learn the basics of posture, hand position and tone production, ideally checked by a teacher or a video lesson.

steps.title: Reading music and basic theory
steps.description: Notes on the staff, rhythm values, time signatures and key signatures. Read a little every day.

steps.title: Scales and arpeggios in the first keys
steps.description: Start with the easiest keys, slowly and evenly, then widen the range and add keys one at a time.

steps.title: Rhythm and tempo control with a metronome
steps.description: Clap and play rhythms, subdivide the beat and raise the tempo in small steps only when the passage is clean.

steps.title: Learn your first complete piece
steps.description: Break the piece into short sections, practise each slowly, join them and play the whole piece from start to finish.

steps.title: Ear training: intervals, chords and playing by ear
steps.description: Recognise intervals and chord qualities, sing before you play and pick out simple melodies without sheet music.

steps.title: Record yourself and get feedback
steps.description: Record a run-through, listen critically and ask a teacher or an experienced player for feedback. Pick two things to fix.

steps.title: Perform for someone
steps.description: Play the piece for a friend, a teacher or an open session. Performing reveals what practice hides.

competencies.name: Technique
competencies.description: Posture, tone, accuracy and economy of movement.

competencies.name: Rhythm and tempo
competencies.description: Keep a steady pulse and play cleanly at the target tempo.

competencies.name: Reading music
competencies.description: Read and play notation at sight at a comfortable level.

competencies.name: Ear training
competencies.description: Recognise intervals, chords and melodies by ear.

competencies.name: Repertoire
competencies.description: Pieces you can play from memory or without stopping.

competencies.name: Musical expression
competencies.description: Dynamics, phrasing and character: playing music, not just notes.

cards.front: Order of sharps in key signatures
cards.back: F, C, G, D, A, E, B (Father Charles Goes Down And Ends Battle).

cards.front: Order of flats in key signatures
cards.back: B, E, A, D, G, C, F: the sharps in reverse.

cards.front: How many semitones in a perfect fifth?
cards.back: 7 semitones, for example C up to G.
Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half steps.

cards.front: What does a 4/4 time signature mean?
cards.back: Four beats in every bar, and a quarter note gets one beat.
Allegro: fast and lively. Andante: at a walking pace. Adagio: slow and at ease.

cards.front: Dynamic marks: p, mp, mf, f
cards.back: Piano (soft), mezzo piano (moderately soft), mezzo forte (moderately loud), forte (loud).

cards.front: What is the relative minor of C major?
cards.back: A minor. It shares the key signature and starts on the sixth degree of the major scale.
Root, major third (4 semitones) and perfect fifth (7 semitones).
Root, minor third (3 semitones) and perfect fifth (7 semitones).
Slow practice builds accurate, relaxed movement that still works when you speed up. Speed is the result of practice, not the method.
